newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Transavia adds four destinations to network.
newsitem.headline: Transavia adds four destinations to network.

text.p: Dutch Transavia Airlines said on Friday it would start scheduled services to the French city of Nice, Barcelona in Spain, the Portuguese capital of Lisbon and Djerba in Tunisia from March 30.
This will increase the number of scheduled service destinations to 14, the airline said in a statement.

The flights to Djerba will be a twice-per-week service. Transavia, which is 80 percent owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, will fly to Nice and Barcelona three times per week and to Lisbon four times per week.
All flights are to be carried out by Boeing 737s with 149 seats and Boeing 757s with 218 seats.
From March 30, Transavia will also step up the frequency of its scheduled service to the Spanish airports of Alicante and Malaga to seven per week from five.
